actions.justification: Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle element. Patient has septic shock - measuring serum lactate is critical for risk stratification and to guide resuscitation. SSC guidelines strongly recommend measuring blood lactate immediately.

Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle element. Blood cultures MUST be obtained before administering antibiotics to identify causative organism and guide de-escalation therapy. This is a critical sequencing requirement.

Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle element. SSC guidelines recommend administering empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour of septic shock recognition. Patient has penicillin/amoxicillin allergy - must select non-beta-lactam or carbapenem-based alternative. Administer immediately after blood cultures are drawn.
MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: Patient has hypotension (BP 80/45, MAP 57) requiring rapid IV crystalloid at 30 mL/kg. This is the top priority mandatory action not yet completed.

Patient presents with confusion (neurological dysfunction), hypotension (cardiovascular), and SpO2 90% (respiratory) — multi-organ dysfunction must be formally assessed to guide further management and SOFA scoring.
BMP (basic metabolic panel) assesses renal function (creatinine, BUN), electrolytes, and glucose — critical for evaluating organ dysfunction in septic shock and guiding fluid/vasopressor decisions.

Patient has persistent hypotension (MAP 57, below target of 65 mmHg) despite 30 mL/kg crystalloid resuscitation. SSC guidelines recommend norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg in septic shock.
Identifying the source of infection is critical to guide source control and antibiotic stewardship. This can be performed simultaneously with resuscitation efforts.
Chest X-ray is indicated to identify a pulmonary source of infection (pneumonia) and evaluate for fluid overload following 30 mL/kg crystalloid administration, given SpO2 of 90%.
Initial lactate was 5.2 mmol/L (>2 mmol/L). SSC guidelines mandate serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation and assess response to treatment. This is a guideline-required action.

MAP remains at 57 mmHg (target ≥65 mmHg) despite norepinephrine already initiated. Adding vasopressin as a second vasopressor is indicated per SSC guidelines to achieve MAP target and reduce norepinephrine requirements.

Patient has refractory hypotension requiring vasopressors. Arterial line provides continuous beat-to-beat blood pressure monitoring, which is essential for titrating vasopressor therapy and managing hemodynamic instability in septic shock.
Patient remains hemodynamically unstable (MAP 57, HR 115, BP 80/45). Serial vital sign assessment is critical to monitor response to vasopressors and fluid resuscitation already initiated.
Lactate 5.2 mmol/L indicates severe hypoperfusion. Reassessing perfusion status (skin color, capillary refill, urine output) guides adequacy of resuscitation and need for escalation.

Gram-positive bacteremia confirmed on blood culture. CBC will help assess WBC count (severity of infection/leukocytosis or leukopenia), hemoglobin, and platelet count to evaluate for sepsis-associated thrombocytopenia or anemia.

Patient has septic shock with gram-positive bacteremia and lactate 5.2. Coagulation studies (PT/INR/aPTT/fibrinogen) are indicated to assess for disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), which is a serious complication of septic shock.

Central venous access is needed for reliable vasopressor delivery (norepinephrine and vasopressin are running), CVP monitoring, and potential additional medication administration. Patient is on two vasopressors with ongoing hemodynamic instability (MAP 57).

Procalcitonin is useful as a biomarker to guide antibiotic therapy duration and assess treatment response in septic shock. Note patient has penicillin/amoxicillin allergy, so monitoring response to current empiric regimen is important.

Patient remains hemodynamically unstable with MAP 57 mmHg, lactate 5.2, and SpO2 90%. Additional crystalloid fluid bolus is indicated to support ongoing resuscitation per SSC guidelines, as initial 30 mL/kg has been given but patient continues to show signs of hypoperfusion and shock.

MANDATORY action: Patient remains hypotensive with MAP 57 mmHg (target ≥65 mmHg) and is in septic shock. Although norepinephrine and vasopressin have been started, this mandatory bundle action must be formally completed/confirmed to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg per SSC guidelines.
Continuous arterial line monitoring is critical given persistent hypotension (MAP 57), lactate 5.2, and vasopressor use. Provides real-time hemodynamic data to guide vasopressor titration.
Patient has septic shock with lactate 5.2, MAP 57, SpO2 90%, HR 115, positive blood cultures, and requires vasopressors — ICU-level care is mandatory for continuous monitoring and management.

violation_events.description: Action start_vasopressor_if_hypotensive performed 35 min after deadline
